question: the objective markers and arrows of an automated headquarters, and the click that sets them

addresses.name: CUnit::OrderToProvince
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::OrderToProvince(CUnit* this, CMapProvince* province, bool append)
addresses.comment: **CUnit slot 6: a right click on a province with this unit selected.** A unit in a battle is never appended to. Nothing happens for a unit with no brigades, a retreating one, or one with an AI agent on a unit above it. For a land unit outside the battle plan branch: the province it stands in, with `append` clear or no path, posts a CCancelMovementCommand; a province CUnit::CanMoveTo refuses gets the `illegal_selection_projection` effect and the `error` sound; otherwise `legal_selection_projection`, the sound `army_move`, and `CMoveCommand(unit, province id, !append, 0, 0)`. Fleets and wings take branches of their own (`navy_move`, `air_move`), not read through. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. **The battle plan branch**, read 2026-11-09: for a land unit of the player's with an agent (a unit under an agent above it has returned already), selected and above a division: a plain click posts CTogglePlanObjectiveCommand(unit, province); an appending click calls slot 29 (CUnit::SetPlanAxisTo). Either plays `army_move`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-frontline.md, section 7.
addresses.revises: The battle plan branch was named and not read.
addresses.evidence: the branch at 0x5C1E0x..0x5C1E9x read in the decompiler

addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CUnit::SetPlanAxisTo(CUnit* this, int province, char extend)
addresses.comment: **Slot 29.** For a unit with brigades above a division: CPlannedPathFind from the unit's province to the one clicked, or with `extend` and a path already from the end of the plan's path, the new leg going to path2; posts CSetPlanAxisCommand. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-frontline.md, section 7.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_MakeAutomationArrow
addresses.no_signature: __cdecl with four stack arguments the decompiler types loosely; the unit's plan path, the type's name and the object layer are the ones that matter.
addresses.comment: Makes an AutomationArrow or OtherAutomationArrow along a plan's path: each province's centre (z 0 at sea), then a last point a quarter of the last leg further, whole pixels, as a CUnitArrow with progress 1.0. ShowSelection calls it twice per plan and keeps both. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-frontline.md, section 7.
